items.title: Publishing Perspectives launches a course to help publishers navigate the AI age responsibly
items.excerpt: Publishing Perspectives is launching a four-week online course and live seminar series to give publishing professionals practical, up-to-the-moment knowledge of how to implement AI in editorial and production workflows and set organizational guidelines. A concrete signal of how houses are trying to operationalize AI rather than just debate it.

items.title: Substack adds Pangram-powered AI detection tools, but creators can disable them
items.excerpt: Substack has rolled out AI-detection labels powered by Pangram that scan posts for AI-generated text, though writers can switch the feature off. The tool only flags material published after 8:30am PT on July 21 and longer than 100 words - a live test of how AI-authorship labeling reshapes the writing/reading contract for authors.

items.title: Researchers to investigate how editors and publishers actually use generative AI
items.excerpt: University of Melbourne and RMIT researchers have launched a survey of publishers and editors about their real-world use of text-based generative AI (LLMs) in independent publishing, aiming to map how the tools are being applied across the editorial workflow rather than how the industry talks about them.

items.title: ElevenLabs releases an AI-narrated Odyssey voiced by an AI-generated Michael Caine
items.excerpt: Book Riot's roundup flags that AI audio company ElevenLabs has released an officially licensed audio retelling of The Odyssey narrated by an AI-generated Michael Caine voice, reviving the debate over synthetic celebrity narration and the erasure of human audiobook narrators' jobs.

items.title: NYT's Kashmir Hill traces an AI-generated biography back to a retiree who has self-published 450+ AI books
items.excerpt: Journalist Kashmir Hill bought an AI-written biography of herself on Amazon and tracked it to Bill Johns, a 70-year-old retiree who has published over 450 AI-generated books. A vivid look at how generative AI is flooding retail bookshelves with machine-authored nonfiction and what it means for discoverability and reader trust.

items.title: New Edison Research study: audiobook listeners are willing to try AI multi-cast narration and rate it favorably
items.excerpt: A blind Edison Research study found audiobook listeners rated AI multi-cast narration favorably against single human narrators on character-driven scenes, though with notable caveats. A concrete data point on whether synthetic voices can win over listeners as AI narration moves from novelty to shipping product.
